content: Desonide is a topical medication prescribed to alleviate redness, swelling, itching, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It belongs to a class of drugs known as topical corticosteroids. The medication works by activating natural substances in the skin to reduce inflammation, redness, and itching. Desonide is available in the form of a cream, ointment, or lotion, and it is typically applied to the skin two or three times daily. It is important to apply the medication at the same times each day and to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Use desonide exactly as directed and avoid applying more or less than prescribed. Do not use it on other areas of your body or for other skin conditions unless instructed by your doctor. Improvement in your skin condition should occur within the first two weeks of treatment. If your symptoms do not improve during this time, contact your doctor. Shake the lotion well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Desonide is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest the medication. To apply, use a small amount of cream, ointment, or lotion to cover the affected area with a thin, even layer, and gently rub it in. If applying to a child’s diaper area, do not use tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants. Do not wrap or bandage the treated area unless directed by your doctor. If instructed to wrap or bandage the area, follow these steps: 1. Soak or wash the area thoroughly. 2. While the skin is still moist, gently rub the medication into the affected area. 3. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap® or Handi-Wrap®). For hands, plastic gloves may be used; for feet, plastic bags; and for the scalp, a shower cap. 4. Seal the edges of the plastic wrap carefully to ensure it adheres closely to the skin. If the area is moist, leave the edges partially unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. 5. Leave the plastic wrap in place for the duration specified by your doctor, typically no more than 12 hours per day. 6. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrap is applied. Do not discontinue treatment abruptly without consulting your doctor. Desonide may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using desonide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to desonide or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, as your doctor may need to adjust your doses or monitor you for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had diabetes, Cushing's syndrome, circulation problems, or any condition affecting your immune system, such as AIDS or severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome (SCID). If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using desonide, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double amount to make up for a missed dose. Desonide may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: stinging, burning, irritation, peeling, dryness, redness, or itching of the skin. Serious side effects, though uncommon, may include redness, swelling, oozing pus, or other signs of skin infection at the application site, as well as severe rash. Children using desonide may be at increased risk for slowed growth and delayed weight gain. Discuss these risks with your child’s doctor. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store desonide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, such as applying more desonide or using it for longer than prescribed, contact your doctor immediately, especially if you experience unusual symptoms. Overuse can affect your body in various ways. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as they may order tests to monitor your response to desonide. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
